title: Empire of China
capsule: The Empire of China was a brief monarchical restoration proclaimed on 12 December 1915 by Yuan Shikai, who had served as the first president of the Republic of China and sought to reestablish dynastic legitimacy under the title Hongxian Emperor. The announcement triggered immediate opposition from provincial military commanders, who launched the National Protection War; within weeks of the imperial proclamation, Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, and other provinces declared independence, and major powers withheld recognition. Yuan Shikai cancelled the monarchy on 22 March 1916, reverting to republican titles; he died on 6 June 1916, leaving China to fragment into the Warlord Era.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The nominal territorial claim was the entire Republic of China, but effective imperial control was contested from the outset; the territorial footprint reflects claimed rather than administered space.
